A case of bleeding requiring hospitaliza- tion that was likely caused by an interaction between warfarin and levamisole. Clin Pharmacol Ther 1996; 59: 360–2. Lipid regulating drugs. Fibrates have been reported to interact with coumarin anticoagulants. Clofibrate can enhance the activ- ity of warfarin, sometimes to the point of haemorrhage. The mechanism of this interaction is not clear, but it does not appear to be a pharmacokinetic effect. Similar enhancement of activity has been reported with clofibrate and dicoumarol or phenindi- one. Bezafibrate has been reported to enhance the effect of phenprocoumon1 and warfarin,2 and fenofibrate3 and gemfibrozil4 have been reported to enhance the effect of warfa- rin, although a study5 in healthy subjects found that gemfibrozil slightly decreased plasma-warfarin concentrations. Interactions may also occur between statins and coumarin anti- coagulants,6 although there have been conflicting reports in some cases. Hypoprothrombinaemia and bleeding has been re- ported in 2 patients on warfarin given lovastatin.7 An increased response to warfarin has also been reported6,8,9 in a number of patients taking fluvastatin. A study10 with rosuvastatin and war- farin reported an increased INR in healthy subjects and in pa- tients on long-term warfarin therapy, although another study11 found no effect. However, there have been reports of haematoma and raised INR in patients after addition of rosuvastatin to long- term therapy with warfarin12 or acenocoumarol.13 An increased response to warfarin has been observed with simvastatin,14 in- cluding a fatal cerebral haemorrhage in a patient who was changed from atorvastatin to simvastatin,15 and potentiation of the effect of acenocoumarol by simvastatin has also been report- ed.16 However, the INR in another patient on long-term warfarin remained stable on the addition of simvastatin.17 Licensed prod- uct information for pravastatin states that no change in warfarin activity has been seen in patients given both drugs, but there has been a report18 of bleeding in a patient taking fluindione when pravastatin was added. In a study19 of 46 patients on warfarin who had been converted from pravastatin to simvastatin, the mean INR increased, but the median weekly warfarin dose did not differ significantly and no episodes of bleeding were report- ed. Dextrothyroxine increases the anticoagulant effect of warfarin sodium20,21 and dicoumarol.22 Colestyramine has reduced warfarin’s serum concentration23 and half-life24 as well as its activity.23,
